description:
**Surfaced 2026-05-17 by PRINCIPAL during substrate-architecture conversation.** Foundational substrate change: encode the base-vs-custom agent convention so customizations have a canonical home that substrate tools respect. Until this lands, `install.sh --yes` + `apply.sh --yes` can silently overwrite customizations that sit in base-file paths — a real footgun as workspaces start customizing their agent teams.

## The architectural model (PRINCIPAL-declared 2026-05-17)

Each workspace at every nesting level has:
- A **BASE stoa team** — deployed from substrate; canonical; mechanically updatable via install.sh / apply.sh
- Optionally **CUSTOM agents/processes** — workspace-authored; separately maintained; the workspace's stoa team designs + builds these

When substrate ships, BASE files update freely (mechanical apply is safe by construction — base is canonical). CUSTOM files stay put. If custom agents want new substrate capabilities, the cheap path is **re-create custom from current base** (operator + team), not "carefully merge upstream into the customization."

PRINCIPAL's framing on cost: creating new custom agents is cheap, so the typical update path when substrate advances is to regenerate customization fresh from new base rather than integrate.

## Why this is foundational

Today the substrate has:
- Tools for mechanical apply (apply.sh, install.sh) — safe ONLY against base files
- check.sh single-bit DRIFTED verdict — collapses "upstream advanced" vs "you customized" vs "both"
- NO convention for where customizations live → customizations naturally sit at base-file paths → substrate tools destroy them silently

Today's consumer workspaces (ariadne-core-workspace, railway_stoa, sector-4) have NOT yet customized their base agents (verified via apply.sh --yes today returning clean diffs). So the footgun hasn't bitten yet. **But it will the moment any workspace customizes a base agent file** — and the next planned work IS the railway_stoa team building a custom railway agent set.

This ticket MUST ship before the railway_stoa custom team work dispatches. Otherwise the railway custom agents have no canonical home that survives substrate updates.

## Deliverables

### D1 — substrate convention encoded in canon

New section in `substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` (likely in §1-§3 area where the architecture is named, or as a new section near §16 POLYBIUS lifecycle) titled "Base vs custom agents" or similar. Encodes:

- BASE files = deployed from substrate; live at canonical paths (the existing install.sh-deployed paths); always safe for substrate tools to overwrite
- CUSTOM files = workspace-authored; live at the convention-TBD location; substrate tools NEVER touch them
- The cost-of-recreation framing: when substrate advances, prefer regenerate-custom-fresh over integrate-into-customized
- Cross-ref to operating-disciplines.md section for universal-team framing

New section in `substrate/operating-disciplines.md` titled similarly. Same content shape, framed for every seat (not just POLYBIUS).

### D2 — convention path/format chosen by DAEDALUS

DAEDALUS picks one of these candidates (or surfaces a better option):

| Option | Custom agent path | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Subdirectory** | `.claude/agents/custom/CAPTAIN_<MNEMONIC>_<slug>.md` | Clean visual; easy to grep; easy for substrate tools to skip via non-recursive glob | Need to verify Claude Code's agent auto-discovery picks up subdirectory paths |
| **Filename suffix** | `.claude/agents/CAPTAIN_<MNEMONIC>_<slug>_custom.md` | Stays at base path; Claude Code discovery unchanged | Less visually distinct; tool glob pattern more complex |
| **Top-level custom dir** | `.claude/custom-agents/CAPTAIN_<MNEMONIC>_<slug>.md` | Cleanest separation | Claude Code likely doesn't discover agents outside `.claude/agents/` |

Subdirectory is the recommended starting point pending Claude Code discovery verification. DAEDALUS surfaces if discovery doesn't work with subdirectory and falls back to filename suffix.

Same convention applies to:
- `.claude/skills/custom/<skill-name>/` (vs base at `.claude/skills/<name>/`)
- `.claude/templates/custom/*.md` (vs base at `.claude/templates/*.md`)
- Possibly custom MAJOR role files: `.claude/major-custom/MAJOR_<MNEMONIC>.md` or similar (DAEDALUS picks)

### D3 — install.sh respects convention

Update `substrate/install.sh` such that:
- Deploy globs are scoped to base paths only (never deploys to custom paths)
- Per-substitution-line cite-comments reference the base-vs-custom discipline
- Add an explicit check: if base-path file is being deployed AND the corresponding custom-path file exists, log a one-line notice ("custom file at <path> coexists; not touched") — operator visibility

### D4 — check.sh respects convention

Update `substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/check.sh` such that:
- DRIFTED / MISSING / OBSOLETE detection scopes to base paths only
- Custom-path files are out of substrate-tool scope (never flagged)
- Optional: separate output section "Custom files present" showing what customizations exist (operator awareness, not action)

### D5 — apply.sh respects convention

Update `substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/apply.sh` such that:
- Apply operations target base paths only
- `--yes` mode safe by construction (only operates on base; can't destroy custom)
- Cite-comment at the apply-target-glob site explaining the base-vs-custom scoping

### D6 — Documentation in workspace CLAUDE.md template

When `install.sh` deploys substrate to a workspace, the workspace's CLAUDE.md template should include a section explaining:
- "Customize your agents at `.claude/agents/custom/` (or whatever D2 picks)"
- "Anything in base paths will be overwritten by substrate updates"
- "Custom agents persist across substrate updates"

If the workspace already has a CLAUDE.md, install.sh's behavior here needs to be deliberate (append a clearly-marked section? skip if CLAUDE.md exists? surface to operator?). DAEDALUS picks.

## Acceptance (probes — VERA scopes precisely)

- Drop a stub custom agent at the convention path; run install.sh; verify the custom file is preserved (not deleted, not overwritten)
- Drop a stub custom agent at a BASE path (mimicking the silent-overwrite footgun); run install.sh; verify the custom file IS overwritten by the substrate base file (this is the FAILURE MODE the convention exists to make explicit — operator MUST move custom to the right location)
- Run check.sh against a workspace with customizations; verify DRIFTED/MISSING/OBSOLETE applies only to base files; custom files not in scope
- Run apply.sh --yes against a workspace with customizations; verify custom files unchanged
- Verify Claude Code auto-discovers custom CAPTAIN agents at the chosen convention path (subdirectory or suffix) — this is the load-bearing empirical test
- SPEC.md / install.sh comment block / role file all consistently describe the convention

## Out of scope (hard-locked)

- **Migrating any existing customized files** to the new convention. There are none today; no migration needed.
- **Building the railway custom agent team itself** — separate forthcoming arc at railway_stoa, dispatches AFTER this convention lands.
- **Four-category drift classification at check.sh** (the locally-modified × upstream-advanced model from stoa--lyh's Option Small). With base-vs-custom convention, four-category becomes unnecessary — substrate tools only see base; custom is operator-owned. Don't reopen Option Small here.
- **Custom POLYBIUS / PLINY at the MAJOR tier.** Convention applies to CAPTAINs + skills + templates. Whether custom MAJORs make sense is a separate design question; defer.
- **Cross-workspace custom-agent sharing** (e.g., railway_stoa's DEPLOYER reused at sector-4). Maybe later; not in this arc.
- **Auto-generated custom-agent templates / scaffolding.** Operator authors custom agents manually (or via agent-author skill); this arc just establishes where they live.

## §15 N=1 caveat

PRINCIPAL declared the architecture today (project-direction authority). Substrate canon enters off-gate on PRINCIPAL's declaration. The empirical anchor is the upcoming railway_stoa custom team arc — once that ships using the convention, evidence accretes. If the convention turns out wrong-shaped during the railway build, this arc's design can revise.

## Cross-refs

- PRINCIPAL's 2026-05-17 chat declarations: "the substrate is a deployable BASELINE; consumer workspaces customize" + "the base agents can always be safely updated; custom agents need user judgment" + "cost of creating new custom agents is low" + "the railway custom team would be a good example, we need a standard stoa team there to develop a custom set of agents and tools for that project"
- stoa--lyh (Option Small design that punted on four-category classification — superseded by this convention; doesn't need reopening)
- stoa--3cs (bundled-squash; independent; can ship before or after)
- stoa--32b.1 (PRINCIPAL-gate discipline; independent; same theme of "substrate verifies before proceeding")
- stoa--32b.2 (mechanical-script / agent-inspection split; related — the inspection-agent layer becomes the operator-visibility mechanism for custom files post-mechanical-apply)
- Forthcoming railway_stoa custom team arc (dispatches AFTER this arc lands; empirical anchor)

## Honest scope estimate

Larger than Arc 27 (single section), comparable to or larger than Arc 28 (multi-file substrate touches + new skill). Full gauntlet expected: DAEDALUS design + ARGUS audit (LIKELY revisions given architecture sensitivity) + ADA build + VERA + CATO + ZENO + ship. ~1-2h wall-clock estimated based on Arc 28 calibration; could be longer if DAEDALUS surfaces convention-design tradeoffs that need PRINCIPAL adjudication.
